paragraphs: Mentioned in [Beitzah 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.15b.21) as “Rav Tachlifa, brother of Rabbanai Choza'ah.” Hyman cites Dikdukei Soferim for “Rav Tachlifa, father—and some say brother—of Rabbana Choza'ah.” Hyman also cites [the Rif](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Shabbat.44b.2), [the Rosh](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_on_Beitzah.2.4.1) and Shibbolei HaLeket, division 2, section 16.

notes.text: The alternative relations are father and brother of the same named Rabbanai/Rabbana. The names and variants remain separate attestations.

The Bavli reads “brother.” The linked Rif explicitly has “father,” with “brother” as an alternative. The Rosh has the unusual wording בר אבוה in the first clause and “brother” as an alternative. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3218&lang=en) contrasts the brother in the Bavli with the son in the Rif, describing the relationship from Rabbanai’s side. The reading in Shibbolei HaLeket remains as Hyman reports it.
